steps.title: Create a container element with fixed dimensions
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named 'container' that sets its width to 400px and height to 300px.
steps.hint: Use the .container selector and define width and height properties with pixel values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule that defines a container with fixed dimensions of 400px by 300px.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .container selector with width: 400px; and height: 300px; properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a container with fixed dimensions, which is essential for controlling layout and overflow behavior.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both width and height are set to the specified pixel values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the correct class name (.container) and setting both width and height properties with px units.

steps.title: Add content that exceeds the container's dimensions
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a paragraph element that contains enough text to exceed the container's height. Use a class selector for the paragraph.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS rule starting with a class selector like '.content' and add a property that makes the text content long enough to overflow.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a paragraph rule with content that will exceed the container's dimensions, setting up the overflow condition.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the paragraph rule, but make sure it has enough text content to actually overflow the container's fixed height.

steps.title: Apply the overflow property with 'visible' value
steps.instruction: Add the overflow property to your container rule and set its value to 'visible'.
steps.hint: The overflow property controls what happens when content overflows its container. 'visible' is the default value, allowing content to spill outside.

steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have the overflow property set to 'visible', showing the default overflow behavior.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set overflow to visible, which is the default behavior where content spills outside the container.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added 'overflow: visible' to the container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container rule should include 'overflow: visible' to demonstrate the default overflow behavior.

steps.title: Change overflow to 'hidden' to clip excess content
steps.instruction: In your container rule, change the overflow property value from 'visible' to 'hidden'.
steps.hint: Look for the overflow property you added earlier and update its value to 'hidden'.

steps.expectedOutcome: The container will now clip any content that extends beyond its boundaries, hiding the excess.
successCriteria: The container rule includes overflow: hidden;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Changing overflow to 'hidden' successfully clips the content that exceeds the container's dimensions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've changed the overflow property value to 'hidden' in your container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The overflow property should be set to 'hidden' in your container rule to clip excess content.

steps.title: Use overflow: 'scroll' to add scrollbars
steps.instruction: Change the overflow property value from 'hidden' to 'scroll' in your container rule.
steps.hint: Look for the overflow property in your container CSS rule and replace its current value with 'scroll'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will now display both horizontal and vertical scrollbars, allowing you to scroll to see all content.
successCriteria: The container CSS rule has overflow: scroll applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Changing overflow to 'scroll' adds scrollbars to the container, making all content accessible by scrolling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've changed the overflow property value to 'scroll' in the container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've modified the overflow property in the container rule to use 'scroll' as the value.

steps.title: Apply overflow: 'auto' for conditional scrollbars
steps.instruction: Change the overflow property value from 'hidden' to 'auto' in the .container rule.
steps.hint: Modify the existing overflow property in your .container CSS rule to use the value 'auto' instead of 'hidden'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will now automatically show scrollbars only when the content exceeds its dimensions, instead of always clipping it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully changed the overflow property to 'auto'. Now scrollbars will appear only when the content overflows the container.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the overflow property value needs to be exactly 'auto' (not 'scroll' or 'hidden').
steps.feedbackWrong: The overflow property in the .container rule should be set to 'auto' to enable conditional scrollbars.

steps.title: Create a resizable element with the resize property
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named 'resizable-box' that sets resize: both to allow user resizing in both directions.
steps.hint: The resize property controls whether an element can be resized by the user. Use 'both' to allow resizing horizontally and vertically.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule .resizable-box with resize: both will be created, allowing the element to be resized by the user.
successCriteria: The .resizable-box rule exists and includes resize: both.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the resize property to allow user resizing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .resizable-box rule, but it's missing the resize: both property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .resizable-box rule with resize: both wasn't found. Make sure to add the rule with the correct property.

steps.title: Limit resize direction to horizontal only
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the .resizable-box class that sets the resize property to 'horizontal' to allow only width resizing.
steps.hint: Use the resize property with the value 'horizontal' to restrict resizing to the horizontal direction only.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .resizable-box element will only be resizable horizontally (width can be changed, height remains fixed).
successCriteria: The .resizable-box rule includes the property resize: horizontal.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully limited the resize direction to horizontal only. Now the element can only be resized horizontally.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the resize property with the value 'horizontal' to the .resizable-box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .resizable-box rule should include resize: horizontal to limit resizing to the horizontal direction.

steps.title: Limit resize direction to vertical only
steps.instruction: In the .resizable-box rule, set the resize property to 'vertical' to allow only height resizing.
steps.hint: Use the CSS property resize with the value 'vertical' to restrict resizing to the vertical direction only.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .resizable-box element will now only be resizable vertically (height can be changed, width remains fixed).
successCriteria: The .resizable-box rule contains the property resize: vertical.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set the resize property to 'vertical', allowing only vertical resizing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the exact property 'resize: vertical' in the .resizable-box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the resize property with value 'vertical' to the .resizable-box rule.

steps.title: Combine resize and overflow properties
steps.instruction: Update the .resizable-box rule to include both resize: both and overflow: auto properties.
steps.hint: Add both properties to the same CSS rule to make the element resizable in all directions with automatic scrollbars when content overflows.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .resizable-box element will become fully interactive - users can resize it horizontally and vertically, and scrollbars will automatically appear when content exceeds the container size.
successCriteria: The .resizable-box rule contains both 'resize: both' and 'overflow: auto' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully combined resize and overflow properties. The element is now fully interactive with resizing in all directions and automatic scrollbars.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both 'resize: both' and 'overflow: auto' to the .resizable-box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .resizable-box rule needs to be updated. Add both 'resize: both' and 'overflow: auto' properties to create an interactive, scrollable container.
